note: Proposed, not sealed. The operator, in a desk session, after the per-prompt one-script hook was put back. The record in full, with the phases: willows-grove docs/design/one-script/flatten-2026-10-19.md.

decisions.question: Does the Table keep the ai-game-master chain beside the one-script record (forge-convergence §9 row 11)?
decisions.commitment: No. The row is reopened and the one-script record is the one chain. The table's ledger_sink.py, a byte-for-byte copy of the ai-game-master hashing, retires with a tombstone once table results are verdict rows in the record.
decisions.why: SPEC-rival §3 row 2: the row's reasons (isolated boxes, own verifier, the games verify) now hold for the one-script record, which also keeps its head outside the box. The operator: "1 yes".

decisions.question: Does the fleet flatten into one contract its pieces follow, or one pile of code?
decisions.commitment: One pile: one repo, one runtime. The pile is willow-bot (seal D2); Rat stays the one runtime that seats a model (D1).
decisions.why: The operator: "2 one pile"; and earlier: "You could literally smash it into one giant pile of one script, and, my guess is, that it would still do the same job. All of it."

decisions.question: Do the game pieces stay in safe-app-store, where a promoted build lifts into its own repo (rule 8)?
decisions.commitment: No. the-table, catgrid and the game-lab rule helpers the table imports move into willow-bot; for these pieces the decision overrides safe-app-store rule 8. A tombstone at each old path names the new home.
decisions.why: The operator: "2, move into the bot".

decisions.question: Does catgrid give up its xorshift32 generator for the one stream when it moves?
decisions.commitment: No. catgrid moves and keeps both: xorshift32, which its JS port and the APK replay, beside the one stream.
decisions.why: The operator: "3, move and keep both. The game will still be played as a game, just the way it's played is a bit different".
